posts.title: Is WebMCP Only for Agents?
posts.description: WebMCP tools were designed for in-browser AI agents, but each one is a named function with input and output schemas that the page keeps up to date. I built WebMCP Macros, a Chrome extension that calls those tools from block programs with no model in the loop, and used it to answer every letter in a Santa's Workshop demo with four blocks.

posts.title: Does WebMCP `outputSchema` Help Agents Pick Better Tools?
posts.description: Consolidating WebMCP read tools while keeping descriptions under 500 characters hides the fields each tool returns from the agent. Here is what happened when I tested WebMCP's new outputSchema across single-turn lookups, multi-step chains, and multi-turn conversations.

posts.title: Would Fine-Tuning Have Beaten Jev?
posts.description: The third post in my series on describing a classifier with Jev versus training one. This time I fine-tuned BERT on the same Jigsaw toxicity comments. With enough labels it ranks toxic comments better than Jev and the cloud-embedding models, but it needs about 500 labels to pass Jev, a GPU to train, and it misses almost every comment on the two rarest labels.
